NCHS_homicide_rate_1933-1967_transcribed.checks: 1940 appears in both Linder & Grove (6.2) and HIST290_4049 (6.2).
NCHS_homicide_rate_1933-1967_transcribed.caveats: Rates are printed to one decimal, so year-to-year log changes carry rounding error of up to about 1-2%. The ICD-6/7 homicide group (E964, E980-E985) appears to include injury by police intervention, which 1968+ (E960-E969) excludes; to be confirmed. Linder & Grove footnote: homicide includes legal executions for 1921-1929 only.

LinderGrove1943_homicide_constant_area_1.what: Crude homicide death rate per 100,000, all races, for three fixed groups of States (the death-registration States of 1900, of 1910 and of 1920), typed by hand from Linder & Grove (1943), one decimal as printed. For the EXPLORATORY 1900-1932 homicide check only; not used in any confirmatory test.

LinderGrove1943_homicide_constant_area_1.method: Read from the page images in the browser's PDF viewer at 200-400% zoom, overlapping views; reading notes in _transcripts/linder_grove_T17_homicide_reading_notes.txt
LinderGrove1943_homicide_constant_area_1.caveats: One decimal, so early log changes (rates near 1.2) carry rounding error up to about 4-8%. Footnotes put legal executions in 'Other accidents' for 1900-1920 (T17), 1910-1921 (T18) and 1920-1921 (T19); Table 15 says homicide includes legal executions for 1921-1929 only, so the 1920/21 or 1921/22 and 1929/30 changes include a small definition shift. The States of 1900 series jumps in 1905 (1.3 to 2.1) and 1908 (3.0 to 3.9) with no change of area; cause unknown (possibly classification or reporting). 1906 (2.0) was hard to tell from 2.9 at 200%; read as 2.0 at 400%.
